title: Railway Changelog #0309: Free VMs without an account
brief: Railway Changelog #0309 opens free Linux VMs with no account: `ssh railway.new` gets a 2 vCPU/2 GB box with coding agents preinstalled, 60 minutes to build and 24 hours to claim it before deletion. The same edition adds request tracing in Priority Boarding (edge-to-database waterfalls with no code changes) and OpenCode on Cloud Agents for persistent agent VMs.

title: Orca
brief: A free, open-source Agent Development Environment (ADE): run Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor CLI, and other CLI agents in parallel across isolated git worktrees, with a Ghostty-class terminal, in-app diff review, embedded browser, and SSH dev built in. Bring your own subscriptions — agents run side by side without interfering.

title: heddlework
brief: A native, harness-neutral workspace for agent sessions: task graphs, diffs, and durable work across coding agents — Pi first, Codex and Claude next. Very early (~12 stars); expect rough edges.
warning: Very early (~12 stars); expect rough edges.

title: paseo.sh
brief: A free, open-source (Apache 2.0) self-hosted daemon for running Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, OpenCode, and Pi from anywhere — phone, desktop, or web. Agents run on your own machine with your own credentials; optional end-to-end encrypted relay, MCP/CLI/TypeScript SDK, and local-first voice.

title: gpui-kit
brief: Rust GUI components for building cross-platform desktop apps on GPUI (the framework behind Zed). ~14.8k stars — one of the more-starred GPUI component libraries.

title: scenario-labs/skills
brief: Agent skills for Scenario: image, video, audio, texture, 3D, and custom-model workflows over the Scenario MCP, aimed at games, entertainment, and creative verticals. Installs with `npx skills add scenario-labs/skills`; ~450 stars.

title: Detail
brief: A curated gallery of the small UI decisions that make products feel considered — smarter word breaks, corner-morph animations, name-derived placeholders — each shown as a short clip. Curated by Rene Wang; a good reference for stealing micro-interaction ideas.

title: Landbook
brief: A website design inspiration gallery with a large curated collection of landing pages, e-commerce sites, portfolios, and templates, plus boards for saving references. Useful for browsing real-world site design by category.

title: MaxiBestOf
brief: A website design and typography inspiration feed updated every weekday, pairing featured sites with their font stacks (e.g., Geist, Neue Haas Grotesk). A Pro tier adds private collections and HD screenshots.

title: SoulStack
brief: ProxySoul × Empryo: a bundle of skills, agents, an "immune system," and habits for coding agents. Very early (~17 stars); concept-heavy and expect rough edges.
warning: Very early (~17 stars); concept-heavy and expect rough edges.

title: GLiNER2.5-Decide
brief: Fastino's 340M-parameter open-weight model for schema-defined decision-making: feed it text plus typed questions and get valid answers with probabilities, confidence scores, and constraint-feasibility metadata. Apache 2.0, CPU-capable, strong on routing/triage/guardrail tasks. Benchmark figures are vendor-reported and not independently verified.
warning: Benchmark figures are vendor-reported and not independently verified.

title: Isoquant
brief: A new PAYGO inference provider launching with GLM-5.3-Flash at $0.07/$0.20 per 1M input/output tokens with automatic prompt caching; drop-in OpenAI-compatible API, no top-up fees. Its published benchmarks claim the lowest latency and highest throughput versus Together, CoreWeave, Baseten, Fireworks, and Z.ai. Pricing and benchmark figures are vendor-reported and not independently verified.
warning: Pricing and benchmark figures are vendor-reported and not independently verified.

title: Prism Inference
brief: Pay-as-you-go inference with no minimums across serverless, elastic, private and dedicated endpoints, plus batch. Lists per-model rates (GLM-5.3 $1.40/$4.40, Kimi K3 $3/$15 per 1M tokens) and states strict zero data retention — inputs and outputs are never used for training.

title: InferHub
brief: Proxy service that pools AI subscriptions into one API. Shared as "a rly interesting proxy" with per-plan pricing on its site.

title: AIHubMix
brief: Multi-model API with per-model pricing, including a GLM 5.3 coding endpoint. Shared via its GLM 5.3 API pricing page.

title: Surplus Intelligence
brief: OpenAI-compatible inference marketplace that routes each request to the cheapest current offer. Vendor claims ~38% savings via routing; pricing and retention terms weren't independently verified.

title: Kitani
brief: Open inference on independent hardware with a prepaid USD balance — the max request cost is reserved, then settled on completion. API is OpenAI-compatible at api.kitani.ai/v1.

title: Pareto Inference
brief: Pay-per-token inference running on Pareto's own GPUs, including GLM 5.3 Flash. Shared via its pricing page.

title: BytePlus ModelArk
brief: BytePlus's Coding Plan for Claude Code, Cursor, Cline, Kilo Code, Roo Code and OpenCode, covering models like Dola-Seed-2.0-pro, GLM-5.1 and DeepSeek V4. Exact plan prices weren't visible on the promo page.

title: Parasail
brief: Inference provider whose homepage FAQ states explicit zero data retention alongside SLA terms. Surfaced in #providers via a comparisons board post.

title: Inceptron
brief: Inference provider with ISO 27001 certification, GDPR compliance and EU residency. No zero-retention statement was found on its site.

title: Subconscious
brief: Coding plans starting at $100/mo with 60M tokens/day. Shared via its pricing page.

title: FEIHOA
brief: Unlimited AI plans from €6. States prompts and outputs are not used for training, though it may retain data briefly for security, abuse prevention and legal reasons.

title: Crof
brief: Inference provider at crof.ai; public evidence is thin (snippet-based). Third-party substitution allegations seen during research are unverified and not repeated here.
warning: Third-party substitution allegations seen during research are unverified and not repeated here.

title: Real API Pricing
brief: GitHub repo behind the real-api-pricing comparison of actual inference API prices. Its web app is already in this library's web-apps section; this is the distinct source repo.

title: OpenCode Go
brief: Subscription plan for the OpenCode coding agent. Shared with a screenshot of the plan page.

title: SingularityAPI
brief: Inference API; a forwarded announcement noted DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash going live on it.

title: DeepSeek clock
brief: Personal utility page showing DeepSeek's live peak/off-peak status in local time with both models' prices either way. Rates match the official docs.

title: Token Harbor
brief: Inference API with a published pricing page; the sharer noted roughly 3.5x markup on its $10 plan.

title: StreamLake
brief: Kuaishou's AI cloud / model-as-a-service platform with API and SDK integration for online inference. Holds ISO 27001/27017/42001 and MLPS Level 3; no explicit zero-retention statement found.

title: CoreWeave
brief: GPU cloud infrastructure company offering serverless inference APIs, dedicated endpoints and GPU clusters. Infrastructure rather than a retail model API.

title: GMI Cloud
brief: GPU cloud with serverless inference APIs and dedicated endpoints; lists H100 at $2/GPU-hour and H200 at $2.60/GPU-hour.

title: Venice
brief: Private AI chat and API with free entry and paid tiers (Pro $18/mo). Its API carries a zero-data-retention promise.

title: Relace
brief: Coding-focused API (Instant Apply model, code retrieval, embeddings, reranking) rather than general LLM inference. Available via Continue.dev, with a self-host/VPC option.

title: AntSeed
brief: Open market for AI inference with no account or email required and optional TEE-backed providers. That design is not the same as a universal zero-retention promise.

title: Inco
brief: Recently launched its own inference platform, announced on the company blog.

title: Kenari
brief: Indonesian inference API — one API key, paid in Rupiah. Shared via its pricing page.

title: InferenceSaver
brief: Comparison and routing service claiming 40–80% savings on AI inference costs.

title: Nube
brief: Inference API with published per-token pricing. States explicit zero data retention with an upstream no-training clause.

title: Cline Pass
brief: Subscription for Cline's coding agent at $9.99/mo, positioned as 2–5x the quota versus direct API spend. The "5x cheaper than API" phrasing seen in chatter is not verified.

title: Nebius Token Factory
brief: Nebius's pay-per-token hosted inference for open text/vision models (~23 models incl. DeepSeek, Llama, Qwen). New accounts get trial credit; uses separate v1 API credentials.

title: Coral Bricks
brief: High-throughput inference aimed at agents. A forwarded promo code (SUPERINT) covered GLM 5.2 and Kimi K3.

title: Fast Inference
brief: Gateway for AI models and coding agents with provider failover. $9/mo gives $10 gateway credit, $49/mo gives $60, then pay-as-you-go at direct rates.

title: Entrim
brief: $10 in credits plus pay-as-you-go inference. Processes prompts and outputs in RAM only and does not train on them.

title: Merge Gateway
brief: Multi-provider gateway. A Discord-shared "75% off DeepSeek V4 Flash through September 30" promo was not corroborated on its site.

title: sference
brief: Managed inference for open models on European GPUs. Public evidence is snippet-based; details unverified.
warning: Public evidence is snippet-based; details unverified.

title: Unifically
brief: Pay-per-use multi-model API (no subscription) with a $0.20 free balance and per-generation pricing, e.g. $0.03 per image. The sharer called it "sus" — treat vendor claims cautiously.

title: Reflex
brief: Post-trained Kimi K3 served with 6x context at a claimed 490 tokens/sec. Performance claims come from the provider's own page.

title: OpenModels
brief: "The open market for AI tokens", with published plans.

title: OpenRouter
brief: Multi-provider model gateway charging a 5.5% fee, with 50 free requests/day. Shared via its GLM 5.3 provider/pricing page.

title: TensorX
brief: EU-hosted pay-as-you-go inference whose pricing page states verbatim: "all inference is zero data retention."

title: AI Router
brief: Swiss-hosted inference API ("All of AI. One API. Made in Switzerland") with GDPR compliance and data hosted in Switzerland. Flat CHF 39/mo unlimited under a fair-use policy; OpenAI-compatible at api.airouter.ch/v1.

title: B.AI
brief: Inference API documented with DeepSeek-V4-Flash endpoints.

title: OrcaRouter
brief: Zero-markup BYOK router with an open-source self-hostable Lite (MIT); the hosted plan includes free credits. Pass-through per-token pricing, e.g. DeepSeek V4 Flash $0.15/$0.29 per 1M in/out.

title: OpenFerence
brief: Inference API at openference.ai; public evidence is snippet-based only. A Discord claim that its GLM 5.2 "is not even real" is unverified.
warning: A Discord claim that its GLM 5.2 "is not even real" is unverified.

title: wafer
brief: Inference provider, with DeepSeek V4 Flash mentioned on it in later chatter. Surfaced via an X post from @wafer_ai.

title: Fireworks AI
brief: Serverless inference from $0.10/1M tokens (under 4B params), $1 free starter credit, 50% off batch. 100–400+ open models with an OpenAI-compatible API, FireAttention engine, LoRA/RFT fine-tuning and dedicated GPUs.

title: RunInfra
brief: Inference provider; its DeepSeek V4 Flash $0.13/M input price was corroborated. A "1.8¢/M blended" figure seen in chatter is not a list price.

title: Freebuff
brief: Free, ad-supported coding agent (CLI, desktop, web, cloud, chat) powered by open models like DeepSeek V4 Pro/Flash and MiniMax M3. Explicit no-training stance — it doesn't share data with third parties that would train on it.

title: GripHubRouter
brief: Cheap pay-as-you-go multi-model router, reportedly built by the sharer's friend.

title: Melious
brief: EU-hosted pay-as-you-go inference; the sharer cited ~240 tok/s on DeepSeek V4 Flash. States it does not train on user data.

title: SiliconFlow
brief: One OpenAI-compatible API for open and commercial LLMs with serverless pay-as-you-go and dedicated endpoints. Homepage claim: "No data stored, ever."

title: CheaperInference
brief: Pay-as-you-go inference with published example rates. Prompt and response bodies are not logged, with zero data retention on supported routes.

title: Novita
brief: Inference provider, mentioned as a fan-out target in routing chatter.

title: Command Code
brief: GOAT plan — $10/mo for $70 in credits (limits $14/5h, $35/week, $70/month) across 30+ open and closed models. No zero-retention statement found.

title: DeepSeek
brief: DeepSeek's official API pricing: pay-as-you-go with 50% off-peak discounts (Flash $0.15/$0.60, Pro $0.66/$1.98 per 1M in/out on cache miss; peak is 2x). The $0.13/$0.30 figures seen in Discord are stale.

title: YOLO Auto
brief: Unlimited-token API plans, currently $19/$39 — the Discord-era $6/mo claim is superseded. Shared as an unlimited Qwen3.6-35B API.

title: Claudin.io
brief: Flat-rate API keys for coding agents, $9–$99.

title: regolo.ai
brief: European inference platform with EUR per-token pay-as-you-go (e.g. Llama-3.3-70B €0.60/€2.70 per 1M in/out) and 70% off the first 3 months. Marketing claim: "Zero data retention on European green infrastructure."

title: Arli AI
brief: Inference API with unlimited-request plans and an explicit zero-logging statement. The sharer noted it seemed new and unstable.

title: Hetzner
brief: Hetzner's free experimental open-weight LLM inference API (announced July 2026), EU-hosted. Roughly 4M input / 100k output tokens per 60s per key, no SLA — not for production.

title: Synthetic
brief: Inference provider; a forwarded announcement covered its scaling of Kimi K3.

title: Aster
brief: OpenAI-compatible inference with free, Pro and Max tiers. States zero data retention on the free tier; Pro around $20 for $30 in tokens.

title: Featherless
brief: Open-model inference provider. Only its status page was visible during research.

title: Meituan LongCat
brief: Meituan's LongCat with Token Packs — 50M tokens for $4.90 (promotion corroborated). Surfaced via an X post.

title: DeepInfra
brief: Pay-as-you-go inference across 100+ models with explicit zero data retention. Example: GLM-5.3 Flash $0.075/$0.25 per 1M.

title: CheapestInference
brief: Flat-rate unlimited time-block subscriptions — Core pool from $22/mo per 8-hour daily block, Frontier $71/mo, Flagship $199/mo. Prompts and completions are processed in memory and discarded, never used for training.

title: PrivacyWatch
brief: Open-source comparison of 86+ provider families (97 surfaces) on training, retention, zero-retention and data location, quoting each provider's own ToS and privacy docs. Maintained by the same crew as this library.

title: OpenAI API pricing
brief: OpenAI's official per-1M-token pricing page (e.g. gpt-6-luna $0.10 in / $0.50 out short-context). Useful as the first-party reference behind third-party price comparisons.

title: Zro
brief: $20/mo including $60 of inference spend, OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible. Explicit zero request retention — prompts and completions are never used for training, evaluation or analytics.

title: InferX
brief: Pay-as-you-go inference across 200+ one-click production-ready model endpoints.

title: xKiro
brief: Unified gateway — free tier with 40+ free models and 5M tokens/day (no card), pay-as-you-go about 35% below official prices on select models. 90+ models across 16 providers on one API key.

title: StepFun
brief: StepFun's open platform with a usage-billed API (api.stepfun.ai/v1) and a 15-day trial needing no card. Serves Step 5 Preview and StepAudio 3.

title: Phoenix Grove
brief: Coding-plan provider; the sharer noted a vague allowance but a free month on offer.

title: Neuralwatt
brief: $10/kWh pay-as-you-go (or per-token), $1 free credit after adding a payment method; monthly plans $20–$200. Hosted multi-model OpenAI-compatible API plus on-prem deployment; 14 models.

title: Chutes
brief: Inference provider that was notably early serving Kimi K3, per channel chatter.

title: Telnyx
brief: Inference API with published per-token pricing — Kimi K3 at $2.70/M input, $0.27/M cached input, $13.50/M output. The sharer noted they're open to negotiating volume pricing.

title: Charm Hyper
brief: Free monthly credits plus a $20/mo plan, with an explicit zero-data-retention and GDPR claim.

title: TokenWatch
brief: Live price comparison across inference providers, maintained by the same crew as this library. The sharer noted a Hyper subscription yields $12.50 of inference a day.

title: Zyloo
brief: Subscription-based inference provider at zyloo.io.

title: Moonshot platform docs
brief: Moonshot AI's platform documentation for the Kimi model family. Shared originally via a Kimi-K3 Hugging Face link.

title: Verboo Code
brief: Free trial, then unlimited-token subscriptions from Junior $24/mo to Ultra $269/mo, plus a usage API from $0.12/1M input tokens. Coding agent plus OpenAI-compatible API on Brazilian servers; states it does not train on or review code and calls.

title: Makora
brief: Inference provider and optimization service — Starter $20/mo and Developer $200/mo (both shown sold out), with private model serving and on-prem options. Starter covers unlimited models under 40B parameters.

title: Loop Library (ForwardFuture Signals)
brief: A library of 85 copy-pasteable AI agent "loops" from ForwardFuture — repeatable workflows like the docs sweep, the architecture-satisfaction refactor loop, the production-error sweep, and the SEO/GEO visibility loop — each with explicit checks and stopping conditions. Searchable across engineering, design, content, operations, and evaluation categories.

title: Flue 1.0 Beta
brief: Flue 1.0 Beta announcement — "the open framework for building agents without lab lock-in: write once, deploy..." Details beyond the embed preview are unverified.

title: LMCache
brief: "Supercharge Your LLM with the Fastest KV Cache Layer." The performance claim is the project's and unverified.

title: pi-shell-acp
brief: A Herdr/tmux setup where sibling AI sessions — pi, Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, OMP, Antigravity — can message and spawn each other while keeping their own auth, tools, and transcripts. The repo has since been renamed from pi-shell-acp to "entwurf" and now covers the Agent Client Protocol and MCP agent protocols more broadly.

title: es-git PR #213
brief: A fix by monotykamary — diff.print() (default Patch format) was stripping the +/-/space line-origin prefixes from output; this PR prepends them back.

title: pi-tool-repair
brief: A validate-then-repair extension for pi that fixes common LLM tool-call mistakes (null fields, stringified arrays, wrong field names, anchor bleed) before tools execute. Tom: "technically their tool repair brought over to pi (+ my additions)."

title: fff PR #593
brief: A fix for fff — the /fff-mode override was only stored in an in-memory variable lost on /reload and session restart; this PR persists fff-mode across reloads and session resumes.

title: fff
brief: "The fastest and the most accurate file search toolkit for AI agents, Neovim, Rust, C, and NodeJS." The performance claim is the project's and unverified.

title: ccusage
brief: Analyze coding (agent) CLI token usage and costs from local data.

title: hyperframes
brief: HeyGen's TypeScript framework for generating video from HTML — describe motion with GSAP-style animations, render via Puppeteer/ffmpeg, and expose it to coding agents over MCP. The linked framemd section documents a Markdown-first animation format so agents can author motion graphics programmatically; ~53k stars.

title: MoneyPrinterTurbo
brief: One-click HD short-video generator: feed it a topic or keyword and an automated AI workflow scripts the video, generates subtitles and TTS narration, and renders a finished clip for Reels/Shorts/TikTok. ~126k stars; note the repo docs are largely in Chinese.

title: Cozy
brief: A local-first private journal: entries live as plain files in a folder on your own device — no cloud, no account, no AI reading your diary — with photos, audio, tags, mood/location tracking, and password-lockable journals. Imports from Notion, Day One, Obsidian, and Bear; $49 one-time ($89 forever) for macOS, Windows, iPhone, and iPad.

title: MiniMax M3
brief: MiniMax's M3 announcement — frontier coding capability, 1M context, native multimodality, and a new MSA architecture. All vendor claims, unverified.
warning: All vendor claims, unverified.

title: codex-lb
brief: A Codex/ChatGPT multiple-account load balancer and proxy with usage tracking, a dashboard, and OpenCode compatibility. Tom: "gonna try first."

title: codex-auth
brief: A Zig-written CLI for switching and managing multiple Codex accounts — handy for anyone juggling several Codex subscriptions or auth contexts from the terminal. ~2.7k stars.

title: Zinley
brief: "Built to extend you. 10× your day" — an AI extension of you across every device and person: takes your calls, writes your emails, and more. Vendor claims, unverified.
warning: Vendor claims, unverified.

title: IRIS
brief: IRIS (Intelligent Real-time Input Suggestion) is an open-source shell auto-completion tool positioned as the successor to Fig: a single native Go binary that runs purely on TTY — no Electron, GUI, account, or telemetry — rendering suggestion menus inline in the real terminal, over SSH and inside tmux. It indexes your aliases and shell history, supports AI suggestions via API key or local models, and configures via a TOML file with instant reload. No Windows support, and it can conflict with other autosuggestion plugins (zsh-autosuggestions, atuin), which the README says to disable first.

title: kimi-k3-mlx
brief: An MLX port of moonshotai's Kimi-K3 (2.78T multimodal MoE); the weights are converted from the original release and requantized. Conversion quality is unverified.
warning: Conversion quality is unverified.

title: Hermes Console
brief: A self-hosted AI agent console ("Tu agente AI self-hosted") that thelaggingway is giving a go. The self-hosted claim is unverified beyond the site's tagline.
warning: The self-hosted claim is unverified beyond the site's tagline.

title: OptMem
brief: Permanent memory for AI agents by Victor Taelin: the whole integration is a 426-token prompt plus a single dependency-free Python script installed with one curl command. You paste a `## Memory` block into your agent's AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, then use `memo wake` (read memory at session start) and `memo note` (record one-liners), plus `nap`, `recall`, `zoom`, and `forget`; storage is an append-only log with a rebuildable binary-tree summary cache (1M memories ≈ 608 MB, wake in 0.03s).

title: Content Architecture
brief: A commercial, agent-ready Sanity CMS starter kit in Next.js 16 and Astro 7 editions: a page-builder CMS with in-app Studio, visual editing, draft mode, SEO helpers, a seed dataset, and Plop scaffolding. Its differentiator is agentic-coding workflow support — it ships AGENTS.md plus scoped skills, two preconfigured MCP servers (one reads the running dev server, one drives real Chrome for screenshots/traces), an editable llms.txt, and token-light Markdown versions of every page served to agents via content negotiation. One license per buyer covers unlimited personal, commercial, and client projects; it is a paid product, not open source.

title: nimbus-lite
brief: A free, framework-free AI chat UI kit in vanilla HTML/CSS/JS — open index.html and it runs, no build step or dependencies. It includes a full chat layout with sidebar, live token streaming with blinking caret, Markdown plus syntax-highlighted code blocks with copy buttons, a model picker, and light/dark themes with accent colors; it is front-end only, so you bring your own backend (OpenAI, Anthropic, or a local model). The maintainer sells a fuller Nimbus kit ($19) adding citations, reasoning blocks, tool-call chips, and attachments.

title: worldmonitor
brief: An open-source (AGPL-3.0) real-time global intelligence dashboard: AI-synthesized news briefs, a 3D globe and WebGL flat map, a live Country Instability Index for 31 Tier-1 countries, and cross-stream correlation of military, economic, and disaster signals. It is built for programmatic access too — MCP server, REST API with OpenAPI spec, CLI (`npx worldmonitor`), and Python/Ruby/Go SDKs, with local-AI support via Ollama — and ships as a web app, Tauri desktop binaries, and PWA. AGPL-3.0 copyleft applies, so commercial/SaaS use needs a separate license or AGPL compliance.

title: Amicro
brief: A curated gallery of premium React micro-interaction and transition components built with React and Motion, with layout inspired by transition.dev. It showcases around 36 named interactions — morph, glare shine, magnetic field, text reveal, focus blur, shake, rotate, color-morph buttons — as ready-to-use UI components. Licensing and copy-paste terms are not stated on the page, so reusability is uncertain.

title: pi-dispatch
brief: Runs the pi coding agent as a self-hosted background service: triggered on demand, on a cron schedule, or by GitHub/GitLab issues, comments, and pull/merge requests, each job executing in a locked-down ephemeral container with a durable queue. It enforces per-job/daily/weekly/monthly spend caps before a single token is spent, and ships a live admin panel with run history, cost insights, and per-trigger spend analytics; MIT-licensed. Note: the bare npm name `pi-dispatch` belongs to an unrelated package — the scoped `@edgehero/pi-dispatch` is the correct install.

title: Componentry
brief: Beautiful animated UI components for React. Rykuuun shared it as a front-end dev finding; details unverified beyond the site's tagline.
warning: Rykuuun shared it as a front-end dev finding; details unverified beyond the site's tagline.

title: Mint Playground
brief: The public gallery for Mint's 3D-asset-creation tooling for AI agents: use Codex, Claude, or Cursor (via the Mint MCP server and Mint Skills) to generate, rig, and animate 3D models, build 3D worlds, and create PBR materials and asset packs. The playground showcases dozens of agent-built interactive 3D scenes, from mini-games to product configurators and data visualizations — though it is primarily a showcase for Mint's tooling rather than a tool you operate directly.

title: delphitools
brief: A handmade-web collection of small, single-purpose browser tools: colour utilities (contrast checker, palette generator/extractor, Tailwind shade scales), image tools (compressor, converter, background remover, favicon generator, SVG optimiser, metadata stripper), plus audio/video and typography tools. Everything is free with no logins, no paywalls, and no data collection; fully open source (0-BSD), with a native iOS app and an offline CLI offering the same tools.

title: modly
brief: An open-source desktop app (Windows, Linux, Apple Silicon macOS) that turns a photo or text prompt into a 3D mesh using open-source AI models running entirely on your own GPU — no cloud inference. It ships an extension system for swapping in models like Hunyuan3D 2 and TripoSG, node-based generation workflows, and a CLI so agents and scripts can drive generation headlessly; MIT-licensed, around 7.7k stars.

title: img2threejs
brief: A skill for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) that rebuilds the object in a reference photo as a code-only, procedural Three.js model — reconstruction-by-code, not photogrammetry or mesh extraction — with a staged sculpting pipeline (blockout → material → lighting → optimization) and vision-review quality gates. It is deliberately token-efficient: deterministic scripts handle validation while model tokens are spent only on visual judgment and code; Apache 2.0, around 16.7k stars, with a live demo gallery.

title: pi-openai-server-compaction
brief: Shared without description; the name suggests an OpenAI-compatible server with context compaction for the pi agent. Unverified.
warning: Unverified.

title: Fractal (Plasma AI)
brief: Plasma AI's Fractal wraps Claude Code and Codex in bounded recursive loops. Details beyond the truncated preview are unverified.
warning: Details beyond the truncated preview are unverified.

title: freerange
brief: From chenglou (React core team alumnus): a static verifier that checks ordinary TypeScript layout code at compile time, without a layout engine. ~650 stars.

title: 60fps.design
brief: An endlessly browsable gallery of ~2,000+ UI/UX animation shots from best-in-class mobile and web apps — buttons, sheets, onboarding, loading states, micro-interactions — tagged across 108 filters. Useful swipe-reference for motion details before implementing your own.

title: pi-queue-steer
brief: A pi extension adding a Cursor-style visible follow-up queue: pending agent tasks are listed, inline-editable, and steerable from a terminal UI while pi works. Small repo (~35 stars) but fills a real gap in agent-driven workflows.

title: pi-grok
brief: Use your x.com Premium/SuperGrok subscription in pi with OAuth login, auto-refresh, and live model discovery; supports grok-4.5, grok-composer-2.5-fast, grok-build, grok-4.3, and x_search. Feature claims come from the repo description and are unverified.
warning: Feature claims come from the repo description and are unverified.

title: Kimi-Vendor-Verifier
brief: A vendor verifier from MoonshotAI; baanish asked if anyone has run it. Details unverified from the message text.
warning: Details unverified from the message text.

title: agentic_coding_flywheel_setup
brief: An agentic coding setup that Rykuuun found "more flexible" than alternatives. Details unverified from the message text.
warning: Details unverified from the message text.

title: tailscale-shell

brief: SponsorBar — puts a small ad in your menu bar and shares the revenue with you ("make money from your menu bar for doing nothing"), with a 10%-extra launch promo. A real launched product, though a niche one.

title: Factory Open Source AutoWikis
brief: Browse Factory-generated wikis for popular open-source repositories — a preview of what living documentation looks like on real codebases before running it on your own. Nice for evaluating doc-generation tooling.

title: monocode
brief: A GUI for your coding agents. Description is minimal, but a visual front-end for agent harnesses is a gap worth filling.

title: synthetic-search-mcp
brief: A search MCP server from baanish, who vouched for PR #4 personally. The shared link was the PR; normalized to the repo root.

title: pi-claude-agent-sdk
brief: An inference provider that lets Pi (a terminal agent harness) run on Claude Code Pro/Max subscriptions instead of API keys. Kenn is using a fork and admits he "just closed my eyes and let the agent figure it out" — expect rough edges.
warning: Kenn is using a fork and admits he "just closed my eyes and let the agent figure it out" — expect rough edges.

title: pi-claude-bridge
brief: Lets you route Pi's model calls through a Claude subscription ("allow sub usage in pi"). Same cost-saving idea as pi-claude-agent-sdk: agentic coding without per-token API billing.

title: spirula-studio
brief: Cross-vendor 3D Gaussian Splatting trainer — video to splat to mesh, running on Vulkan or CUDA. Notable for not being CUDA-locked.

title: Responsively App
brief: A dedicated browser for responsive web development — preview a site at multiple screen sizes side by side. Built for faster, more precise responsive work.

title: Grokbot Characters (Rege Lab)
brief: A Rege Lab page with six little Grokbot character expressions to play with, plus downloadable editable CoAnimato files. A creative asset resource for bot and character design.

title: Getting the most out of Opus 5.5
brief: Official Claude guide to prompting Opus 5.5, steering long agent runs, and checking results in Claude apps and Claude Code. A practical reference for anyone driving long agent sessions.

title: Grokbot Icon Studio
brief: A minimal bot-icon studio — browse bot icon examples and copy a prompt to generate an icon of your own. Quick asset generation for bot projects.

title: Cloudflare Quick Tunnels
brief: Cloudflare Quick Tunnels — free encrypted tunnels that expose localhost as a public URL. Cata plans to use it instead of the VS Code tunnel.

title: BendSR
brief: Symbolic regression implemented in Bend. A research-flavoured repo for anyone exploring the Bend language.

title: security-audit-skill
brief: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings. A drop-in skill for agentic security reviews.

title: Saving 100TB of RAM with math
brief: Cloudflare engineering deep-dive on saving 100TB of RAM with math (and Rust). A solid systems-engineering read.

title: Bend
brief: Bend 2 — a fast programming language that blocks AI mistakes via proof checking. Install with curl from bend-lang.com.

title: Monid free agent search (announcement)
brief: Announcement of a free agent search/fetch API — "killed Exa, Tavily and Brave", $0 with no quotas, from Tiny_Fish and MonidHQ. The pricing claims are the poster's and unverified; this link is the announcement, not documentation.

title: jev-search
brief: Shared by thelaggingway with just "Another one" — context is thin, but it landed in the search-tool thread. Worth a look if you're tracking search APIs.
